dedupe_keys.name: san francisco public water assets restrooms and drinking fountains

description: A growing list of the public water assets managed by the City and County of San Francisco, published on DataSF by the Public Utilities Commission. The data are split into two categories, restrooms and drinking water, and combine asset information from several departments, including Recreation and Parks, the Public Utilities Commission and Public Works, into one data model regardless of owner or location. The city says it can be used to locate restrooms and drinking fountains across the city and to feed maps. Records are geocoded by latitude and longitude. Coverage: San Francisco. Update process: as needed, published monthly; the portal shows the dataset first published on 27 February 2025 and last updated on 1 September 2026, and lists related datasets on recreation and parks facilities and the COVID-19 pit stops. Access: open download and API. Licence: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License; cost free. Caveats: the list is described as growing, so coverage of assets is incomplete, and it carries locations and types, not usage or condition. Useful for public space accessibility, heat and emergency response planning, for example siting hydration points; related records are not yet linked.
